title: Opal Systems POC — Security QA Workbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This workbook captures the security and compliance artifacts, questionnaire responses, and workshop notes from the Opal Systems POC (November 2025–January 2026). The goal is to provide a single reference for the customer security champions and our internal teams (SEs, Security, SRE) to close open evidence gaps and prepare a compact audit bundle if Opal advances to Dedicated or Private deployment.

High-level summary:
- Customer: Opal Systems (mid-market healthcare analytics)
- Engagement type: Solutions Engineering POC (data-in-transit and data-at-rest controls, tenant isolation tests, KMS/HSM gating)
- Primary ask: Demonstrate private deployment with customer-managed KMS, network isolation, and SOC2-like evidence for controls mapping
- Current readiness: majority of technical artifacts available; outstanding items primarily process artifacts (retention policies, on-call escalation runbook) and one test capture for HSM key import procedure.

Workshop timeline and attendees:
- Kickoff workshop: 2025-11-05 — SEs, Opal security lead, SRE, Security PM
- Evidence triage workshop: 2025-12-10 — Samira Venkatesh (SE lead), Marcus Li (Security Engineer), Priya Shah (SRE), Opal: Claire Donovan (security lead), Tom Ruiz (platform)
- Final readiness review: 2026-01-08 — internal gate review, determined items to include in production handoff bundle

Attendee list (for record):
- Samira Venkatesh (Redwood, Solutions Engineering)
- Ethan Cole (Redwood, Product Security)
- Lena Martín (Redwood, Customer Success)
- Priya Shah (Redwood, SRE)
- Marcus Li (Redwood, Security Engineer)
- Claire Donovan (Opal Systems, InfoSec)
- Tom Ruiz (Opal Systems, Platform)

Questionnaire response highlights (concise):
- Data classification: Customer will classify datasets; Redwood provided recommended classification matrix and default network ACL templates. Evidence: evidence/opal-data-classification-template.xlsx (provided)
- Access controls: RBAC implemented at API and console level; request logs captured in centralized logging (retention configurable). Evidence: logs/opal-rbac-demo-2025-12-09.txt and screenshots/rbac-console-2025-11-05.png
- Key management: Customer-managed KMS integration validated for read/write encryption keys using Redwood Private build. Evidence: KMS/key-rotation-demo-2025-12-18.mp4; HSM import attempt captured in evidence/hsm-key-import-try1.log (note: the HSM import test failed due to vendor agent version mismatch; remediation planned).
- Network isolation: VPC peering and private endpoints demoed; IP allowlist and mutual TLS on control plane documented. Evidence: network/peering-setup-terraform.txt; screenshots/vpc-flowlogs-2025-12-11.png
- Audit logs and retention: System emits structured audit events; default retention 90 days for high-volume tenants. Evidence: logs/audit-sample-2025-12-10.ndjson
- Penetration test status: No full pentest completed for the POC; recommended next step is a scoped pentest prior to production Dedicated deployment.

Control-to-evidence mapping (selected controls):
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+ enforced; mTLS for private control plane — evidence: network/tls-mtls-summary.txt, screenshots/mutual-tls-2025-12-10.png
- Encryption at rest: AES-256 with envelope encryption when KMS is configured — evidence: KMS/key-rotation-demo-2025-12-18.mp4, config/encryption-policy.yaml
- Key custody: Customer KMS can be used; HSM import test logs in evidence/hsm-key-import-try1.log (follow-up required)
- Identity and access management: RBAC, service principals, and short-lived tokens — evidence: logs/opal-rbac-demo-2025-12-09.txt, screenshots/iam-policy-export-2025-11-07.png
- Network controls: VPC peering, private endpoints, egress rules — evidence: network/peering-setup-terraform.txt, screenshots/vpc-flowlogs-2025-12-11.png

Outstanding evidence and risks (actionable list):
1) HSM import validation — test failed; need a second run with updated vendor agent (target: 2026-01-22). Owner: Marcus Li.
2) Retention policy formalization — customer-facing PDF describing retention defaults and customization steps (owner: Lena Martín, due: 2026-01-20).
3) On-call escalation runbook — internal SRE runbook for Opal POC incidents (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2026-01-18).
4) Commerce & billing isolation note — provide confirmation that customer usage is segregated from other tenants in billing records (owner: Ethan Cole, due: 2026-01-25).

Evidence indexing (how artifacts are organized for handoff):
- evidence/ (technical captures, logs, screenshots, videos)
  - evidence/hsm-key-import-try1.log
  - evidence/opal-data-classification-template.xlsx
  - evidence/KMS/key-rotation-demo-2025-12-18.mp4
  - evidence/audit-sample-2025-12-10.ndjson
- config/ (config samples used during POC)
  - config/encryption-policy.yaml
  - config/iam-policy-sample.json
- screenshots/ (UI captures)
  - screenshots/iam-policy-export-2025-11-07.png
  - screenshots/vpc-flowlogs-2025-12-11.png
- logs/
  - logs/opal-rbac-demo-2025-12-09.txt

Note: The directory names above reference artifacts included in the POC bundle that will be zipped for Opal. Filenames are samples — final bundle will include hashes and timestamps.

Workshop notes and decisions (raw):
- 2025-11-05 Kickoff: Customer requested explicit documentation showing where raw customer prompts are (not stored by default). We confirmed runtime only stores ephemeral KV cache in memory unless configured for debugging; added a task to produce a short explainer for debugging snapshots (Samira action).
- 2025-12-10 Evidence triage: Decided to defer pentest until production sign-off; agreed to run a scoped threat-model exercise and produce a risk memo. Agreed scope items: KMS/HSM, network egress, data retention.
- 2026-01-08 Final review: Verified that all technical artifacts are present; prioritized process docs for closure. Customer happy to accept evidence bundle with identified follow-ups.

Customer-facing summary (one paragraph):
We have completed a compact security validation for the Opal Systems POC: Redwood demonstrated private deployment networking, RBAC and audit logging, and customer-managed KMS integration. Technical evidence for the majority of controls has been collected and packaged. Outstanding items are limited to an HSM import re-test and a few process-level playbooks; we propose these be completed before production cutover.

Attachments to include in the final POC bundle (recommended):
- evidence.zip (contains all logs, screenshots, videos listed above)
- opal-poc-security-responses.pdf (formatted questionnaire responses)
- opal-poc-evidence-index.csv (manifest with SHA256 hashes)

Follow-up plan and owners (timeline):
- 2026-01-15: Share draft evidence bundle with Opal (Samira)
- 2026-01-18: Deliver SRE on-call runbook (Priya)
- 2026-01-20: Publish retention policy docs (Lena)
- 2026-01-22: HSM import validation re-run (Marcus)
- 2026-01-25: Finance/billing isolation confirmation (Ethan)

Useful references and links (internal):
- Confluence: OPAL-POC-Runbook (link in linked_artifacts)
- Jira epic: JIRA-SEC-4021 (evidence remediation tasks)
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/718 (private endpoint helpers)

Notes to internal reviewers:
- Keep the artifact bundle minimal and redacted for PII; do not include raw customer data unless explicitly cleared.
- Ensure each evidence file has a short README entry explaining what it demonstrates and which control it maps to (this will speed up customer review).
- Consider scheduling a 30-minute follow-up workshop with Opal security team after HSM re-test to close their gating questions.

Document history:
- 2025-11-02: initial draft created by Samira Venkatesh
- 2025-12-12: evidence triage updates by Marcus Li and Priya Shah
- 2026-01-08: final review notes added after gate
- 2026-01-15: prepared for customer delivery

End of workbook.
